The given graph shows changes in the air pressure of lungs during breathing. What causes the change in air pressure during period X?

(The figure is a graph of "Air pressure in the lungs (kPa)" on the vertical axis against "Time" on the horizontal axis. During the interval marked X at the start, the trace falls to a trough — the lung air pressure decreases — before rising again to a peak.)

options.label: A
options.text: Movement of ribs downward and inward

options.label: C
options.text: Relaxation of the external intercostal muscles

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease in the volume of the lungs

subject: Biology
stem:
All members of the Gupta family can roll their tongue. Which of the parts labelled in the given figure carries the information regarding this characteristic?

(The figure is a diagram of a nucleus. A dense rounded body inside is the nucleolus; a network of fine threads fills the interior (chromatin/DNA); the boundary is the nuclear envelope, studded with pores and continuous with rough endoplasmic reticulum. Label P points to the upper envelope/nucleolus region, label Q points to the thread network (chromatin), label R points to the membrane projections on the right, and label S points to the nuclear envelope at the bottom.)

subject: Biology
subtopic: Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
stem:
The given figure shows a food web in a forest area. In the forest, large amount of insecticides are blown with wind from a nearby field. What will be the effect on the given food web?

(The food web shows: Trees → Flies and Trees → Caterpillars; Flies → Frogs and Flies → Sparrows; Caterpillars → Sparrows; Frogs → Snakes; Sparrows → Snakes and Sparrows → Hawks. Insecticides kill the insects — the flies and caterpillars, which are the primary consumers.)

options.label: A
options.text: Greater reduction in the number of caterpillars than in the number of flies

options.label: B
options.text: Reduction in the number of hawks and snakes

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in the number of frogs

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in the number of sparrows

subject: Biology
stem:
The figures above are drawn from slides showing reproduction in Yeast and Amoeba. The correct description of the above is:

(Two figures. The left figure is an irregular Amoeba-shaped cell whose nucleus has stretched into an elongated dumb-bell across the cell, but the cell itself is not yet constricted. The right figure is a rounded Yeast cell carrying a small bud at the top, the bud already having its own nucleus.)

options.label: A
options.text: Amoeba undergoing cytokinesis and Yeast undergoing budding.

options.label: B
options.text: The nucleus of a parent Amoeba is undergoing division to pass into its bud while Yeast has already divided into two daughter cells.

options.label: C
options.text: Amoeba undergoing binary fission but at a stage when nucleus is elongating, while Yeast has undergone budding.

options.label: D
options.text: Yeast undergoing binary fission and daughter nuclei have already formed, while a newly formed daughter Amoeba is undergoing growth.
